sourceChallenges.finding: The response actually integrates molecular/cellular mechanisms, proteins/carbohydrates/lipids/metabolism, bacterial/protein/DNA laboratory work, digestion, calculus/linear algebra/statistics, product needs/specifications/prototypes/consumer research, biopolymer experiments, lifecycle assessment and farming/circular systems. sourceChallenges.question: Do sequential alternatives and rejection have sufficient substantive grounds?
sourceChallenges.finding: WUPEB’s neuroscience/sensory/consumer/behaviour-change focus is materially supported by regulatory neurobiology/eating-disorder and sensory mechanisms, health/social psychology, physiology and consumer methods. The third direction materially changes to agricultural ecosystems, soils/water, resources and environmental governance/economics. Animal-origin is individually assessed: husbandry/aquaculture/alternative proteins and allergy/biology foundations exist, but no distinct cumulative meat/milk/insect product-quality/processing/food-allergy curriculum is supplied. It is not rejected merely for lacking a degree title or described as wholly absent.

sourceChallenges.question: Are matches based on meaningful shared subjects/methods rather than convenient functions?
sourceChallenges.finding: Yes, with explicit limits. Bacterial/hygiene laboratory foundations do not imply chemical toxicology. Starch-biopolymer preparation and mechanical tests are a specific packaging-material overlap, not food-barrier/safety engineering. Consumer-needs/prototypes/production planning are one meaningful part of product integration, not a food practical. Vectors/matrices and calculus/inference correspond directly; biochemical and digestive foundations are partial. E-waste/metal recovery is not food processing, infection/immunity is not HACCP, generic business is not quality assurance, and research methods are not the thesis.
